name: Teriparatide

lead: Teriparatide is a recombinant fragment of human parathyroid hormone (residues 1-34) used as a daily injection to treat severe osteoporosis. Unlike most osteoporosis drugs, which slow bone loss, it stimulates new bone formation.

It appears in looksmaxxing talk because of speculation that bone-building drugs could enhance jaw or facial bone. There is no evidence for cosmetic skeletal change in healthy adults, and its approval covers osteoporosis only.

paras: Intermittent exposure to PTH fragments stimulates osteoblasts through the PTH1 receptor, increasing bone formation more than resorption in the short term. Continuous exposure instead promotes bone breakdown, which is why the treatment pattern matters. Effects are largest in trabecular bone such as the spine.

Possible effects include nausea, dizziness, leg cramps and raised blood calcium. Osteosarcoma was seen in high-dose rodent studies, which led to a former boxed warning and treatment duration limits. It is prescription-only, expensive and not appropriate for people with certain bone conditions or prior radiation. It is not an approved or evidence-based cosmetic treatment.
